# COIN (Coinbase Global, Inc., NMS): Technical Report as of 2026-11-16

## 1. Bottom line
COIN is in a confirmed, accelerating downtrend and is oversold on a short-term basis. The latest verified close is **119.84**, the lowest close in the 2026-05-18 to 2026-11-16 data I pulled. Every trend gauge is bearish, and no indicator shows a reversal signal yet. Oversold readings in a trend like this are a warning of stretched selling, not a buy signal.

The verified snapshot and the individual indicator calls agree on every shared value, so I found no discrepancies. VWMA is not in the snapshot. Its value (139.75) comes only from `get_indicators` and does not conflict with anything.

## 2. Indicators chosen and why
I selected 8 indicators that cover different dimensions with little overlap:

- **close_50_sma and close_200_sma** give the medium- and long-term trend regime.
- **close_10_ema** gives short-term momentum and the first resistance on a bounce.
- **macd** gives trend-momentum direction. The snapshot also supplies the signal line and histogram.
- **rsi** flags overbought and oversold conditions.
- **boll_lb** marks the volatility-based lower boundary. The snapshot supplies the middle and upper band.
- **atr** is for stop distance and position sizing.
- **vwma** adds volume confirmation, which the other price-only indicators lack.

## 3. Price action (verified OHLCV)
**2026-11-16:**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Open | 119.31 |
| High | 122.98 |
| Low | 117.32 |
| Close | 119.84 |
| Volume | 11,172,766 |

- **Gap down:** The 11-16 open of 119.31 is well below the 11-13 close of 127.65. The session closed 7.81 points (about 6.1%) below the prior close, in the lower part of its range.
- **Selling pressure:** Closes fell from 136.27 (11-11) to 130.67 (11-12), 127.65 (11-13) and 119.84 (11-16).
- **New period lows:** The 11-16 low of 117.32 is below every prior low in the dataset. Earlier lows include 139.18 (06-26), 139.11 (07-31), 135.46 (11-02), 133.50 (11-05) and 125.38 (11-13).
- **Lower highs and lower lows in November:** The rebound high was 153.33 on 11-04. Later highs were 139.75 (11-09) and 138.86 (11-11), all below it.
- **Heavy volume on the breakdown:** 11-16 volume of about 11.2M is above the 5–8M typical of recent sessions. The 10-30 break (close 143.54, volume 20.9M, open 148.23 vs. prior close 160.59) was heavier. The 07-31 selloff on 20.87M volume is the only comparable earlier volume spike.
- **Prior structure:**
  - The 08-19 to 09-21 advance went from 146.23 to a high of 208.33.
  - Closes held in the 183–201 range through 09-22 to 10-06.
  - Price has since given back the whole advance and more.
- **Reference levels (unvalidated):** The 139–142 area (lows on 06-25, 06-26 and 07-31) was broken on 10-30 and 11-02. It may now act as overhead resistance on a bounce, but I have no tool evidence that it has done so.

## 4. Trend: moving averages
| Indicator | 2026-11-16 | Close vs. level |
|---|---|---|
| 10 EMA | 134.65 | Close is 14.81 below |
| VWMA | 139.75 | Close is about 19.9 below |
| 50 SMA | 169.09 | Close is about 49.3 below |
| 200 SMA | 173.68 | Close is about 53.8 below |

- **Full bearish stack:** Price < 10 EMA < VWMA < 50 SMA < 200 SMA.
- **Death-cross configuration:** The 50 SMA is below the 200 SMA (169.09 vs. 173.68). It was already below throughout the 30-day window (177.93 vs. 182.03 on 10-19). The gap has widened slightly, from 4.10 to 4.59 points.
- **All averages are falling.** The 10 EMA dropped from 177.70 (10-19) to 134.65. The 50 SMA went from 177.93 to 169.09 and the 200 SMA from 182.03 to 173.68.
- **Practical reading:** Rebounds are likely to meet resistance first at the 10 EMA (about 134.65), then the VWMA (about 139.75). A move back above the 50 and 200 SMA (about 169–174) would be a much larger trend change and is far from current prices.
- **Caveat:** The 200 SMA needs more history than the 127 rows I pulled. I rely on the vendor and snapshot value, which agree.

## 5. Momentum: MACD and RSI
- **MACD** is -12.75, **signal** -10.89 and **histogram** -1.86 (snapshot). MACD is below its signal with a negative histogram, so there is no bullish crossover. MACD is at the low end of its 30-day range. It was -1.91 on 10-19 and has fallen almost steadily to -12.75, with slight pauses on 11-03 (-9.11 vs. -8.58 on 11-02) and 11-10/11-11 (-11.53, -11.46). It slipped further to -12.02 on 11-13 and -12.75 on 11-16.
- **RSI** is **29.23**, just under the 30 oversold threshold. Earlier in the window it was 31.91 (10-30), 29.70 (11-02) and 32.43 (11-13). It bounced to 40.65 on 11-04, but price still made new lows afterward. A pattern of RSI mostly between about 29 and 36 since 10-30 is typical of a persistent downtrend.
- **Divergence:** I do not see a clear bullish divergence in this data. RSI made a marginally lower low (29.23 vs. 29.70) alongside the lower price low.

## 6. Volatility: Bollinger Bands and ATR
- **Bollinger Bands (snapshot):** lower 114.69, middle 147.88, upper 181.07. The close is 5.15 above the lower band. The 11-16 low of 117.32 did not touch it.
- **The lower band has fallen sharply.** It went from 166.12 (10-19) to 114.69 as volatility expanded. Price is in the lower third of a very wide band (66.38 points wide), well below the 147.88 midline.
- **Band-walk risk:** In strong downtrends price can ride the lower band. The 114.69 level is the nearest volatility-based reference below price, and a close beneath it would signal continued expansion.
- **ATR is 9.61**, about 8% of the close. It peaked in the window at 11.06 on 11-05 and has eased since. The 11-16 true range was about 10.33, because the gap from the prior close of 127.65 down to the 117.32 low exceeds the intraday range. Volatility remains high.

## 7. Volume confirmation: VWMA
VWMA is 139.75, above the 10 EMA (134.65). Volume-weighted prices exceed the simple short-term average, which fits heavier volume on the higher-priced days earlier in the period. The VWMA has fallen from 180.87 (10-19). The heavy-volume sessions (10-30, 11-05, 11-16) were mostly down days. That supports the view that the decline is volume-backed, not drifting.

## 8. Scenarios and risk framework (conditional, not a trade recommendation)
**Bearish continuation (the path of least resistance on current evidence):**
- Triggers are a close below the lower band (about 114.69) and MACD and histogram staying negative.
- Heavy volume on further down days would confirm it.

**Oversold bounce:**
- RSI under 30 and the stretch below the 10 EMA make a relief rally plausible.
- The first hurdles are the 10 EMA (about 134.65), the VWMA (about 139.75) and the 139–142 old-low zone.
- A bounce that stalls below those levels fits the existing downtrend. Confirmation would need a close above the 10 EMA with MACD histogram turning less negative.

**Risk sizing:**
- With ATR at 9.61, a 1.5×ATR stop is about 14.4 points and a 2×ATR stop about 19.2.
- Gap risk is real: the 10-30 and 11-16 sessions both opened sharply lower, so stops may fill worse than planned.
- Position sizes should reflect daily ranges of roughly 8% of price.

## 9. Limits of this analysis
- I have no news or fundamental data, so I cannot attribute the 10-30 or 11-16 drops to any cause.
- I make no claims that any level has acted as support or resistance historically. The reference levels above are only prior price extremes from the data.
- The 11-16 volume (11,172,766) is as reported by the snapshot. If this bar was captured before the session ended, the day's range, close and volume could still change.

## 10. Summary table

| MACD / signal / histogram | -12.75 / -10.89 / -1.86 | Bearish, no crossover |
| RSI | 29.23 | Oversold, but no divergence or reversal confirmation |

My case is that the market is pricing COIN as if the trough is the permanent state, while the evidence says a base is forming in the business, even though the stock hasn't turned.

## 1. The business stopped getting worse in Q3

- **Revenue stabilized sequentially.** Q3 2026 revenue was $1,216M against $1,220M in Q2, a change of -0.3%. After a decline from $1,869M (Q3 2025), a flat quarter is what a floor looks like. The -35% year-over-year figure is mostly the comparison against a strong 2025 base.

The vendor's ~85% gross margin is the key to the torque. If it's right, each incremental dollar of revenue drops through at a high rate, so a modest recovery in crypto volumes moves profit disproportionately. - **Cash:** $8.6B, flat from Q2 to Q3 after the Q2 decline.

The cash drawdown came mostly from financing outflows (about -$2.7B in Q2), and financing turned positive in Q3 (about +$156M). I don't yet know what drove those outflows, and I'd check the 10-Q.
